actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range:
This species is endemic to the Galápagos Islands (Robertson and Allen 2015), including the islands of Darwin and Wolf (Banks et al. 2009). Records from Ecuador and Peru require verification (Bradbury et al. 1999). 

The depth range is 5-300 m (Bradbury et al. 1999, S. Buglass pers. comm. 2022). It occurs deeper in Darwin and Wolf but shallower (typically between 10-30 m) elsewhere in the archipelago.
documentation.population: This species is relatively common from 15 to 20 m depth in the western part of the Galápagos at Fernandina and Isabela and on the northern coasts of Floreana and Española. In the northern islands of Marchena and Wolf, the species can be found at 25 m (F. Rivera pers. comm. 2022). It is also super abundant between 100-200 m at Darwin and Wolf Islands (S. Buglass pers. comm. 2022).
documentation.habitats: This demersal species inhabits sand and coral/rock rubble bottoms and is associated with reef edges (Hubbs 1958, Bradbury et al. 1999). The maximum total length is 25 cm (Robertson and Allen 2015).
documentation.measures: There are no species-specific conservation measures. Its distribution overlaps with the Galápagos National Park.
documentation.rationale: This demersal species can be common and abundant and is endemic to the Galápagos Islands where it occurs over a wide depth range. There are no known major threats; therefore, it is listed as Least Concern.
